title: Dimension of the closure of section values under specialization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $B$ be a finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $p:Y\to T$ be the structure morphism and $(a_i:T\to Y)_{i\in I}$ any set-indexed family of sections, so $p\circ a_i=\mathrm{id}_T$. Suppose $t_0,t_1\in T$ and $t_0\in\overline{\{t_1\}}$. For $j=0,1$, let $Y_{t_j}=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t_j)$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-residue-field] and let $C_j$ be the closure in $|Y_{t_j}|$ of the images of the induced rational points $a_i(t_j):\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t_j)\to Y_{t_j}$ [def-pc-rational-point]. Then $\dim C_1\geq\dim C_0$, with topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The index set may be empty, in which case both dimensions are $-\infty$. No flatness, smoothness, separatedness, henselianity or reducedness is assumed.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 7, first assertion, printed p.126 (PDF p.132), affine case. Primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: If $I=\varnothing$, both closures are empty and both dimensions are $-\infty$. If $t_0=t_1$, the two closures agree. Hence assume $I\ne\varnothing$ and $t_0\ne t_1$. The affine scheme $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian: its one-member affine cover has Noetherian coordinate ring [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-sbc-noetherian-specialization-trait] with $(y,x)=(t_1,t_0)$ to obtain a DVR $R$ and $u:\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$, with generic point $\eta$ mapping to $t_1$ and closed point $s$ mapping to $t_0$. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Base change each specified section along $u$; the defining projection identities of [def-pc-base-change] show that these are sections of $Y_R$. The induced maps of residue fields are field extensions $\kappa(t_1)\to K$ and $\kappa(t_0)\to k$.

source.place: Tag 054F, lemma-locally-Noetherian-specialization-dvr; BLR 5.3 Lemma 7, reduction to a DVR.

proof.text: For $j=0,1$ set $B_j=B\otimes_A\kappa(t_j)$, the coordinate ring of $Y_{t_j}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Let $e_{ij}:B_j\to\kappa(t_j)$ be evaluation at the specified section value and put $J_j=\bigcap_{i\in I}\ker(e_{ij})$. In the Zariski topology a closed set $V(L)$ contains every value precisely when $L\subseteq J_j$; thus $C_j=V(J_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], $Z_j=\operatorname{Spec}(B_j/J_j)$ has underlying space $C_j$. Each value factors through $Z_j$, and their images are dense there. The quotient map defines a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion]. After extending the field to $L_1=K$ or $L_0=k$, this remains a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; [lem-sfb-rational-density-field-extension] makes the induced values dense in $(Z_j)_{L_j}$. Its closed image is therefore exactly the closure $C'_j$ of the base-changed values. The images of a fixed finite set of algebra generators of $B$ generate $B_j/J_j$ over $\kappa(t_j)$. Apply [lem-pc-dim-base-change] to this finite type algebra and $L_j/\kappa(t_j)$, and use [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] to identify ring and spectrum dimensions. Hence $\dim C'_j=\dim C_j$. It suffices to prove the assertion over $R$.

source.place: Corollaire 11.10.7, printed p.172; field-extension dimension: Stacks Tag 00P3 (algebra-lemma-dimension-preserved-field-extension).

proof.text: Write $D=B\otimes_A R$ and $F=D\otimes_R K$, and let $e_i:D\to R$ be the maps of the base-changed sections [def-weil-affine-spectrum, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Their generic evaluations are $e_{i,K}:F\to K$. Put $J=\bigcap_i\ker(e_{i,K})$, $H=F/J$, and let $P$ be the inverse image of $J$ under $D\to F$. Set $Q=D/P$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}Q$. The map $Q\to H$ is injective by the definition of $P$. Moreover the map $Q\otimes_R K\to H$ sending $q\otimes c$ to $cq$ is an isomorphism: every element of $F$ can be written $d/a$ with $d\in D$ and $0\ne a\in R$, by taking a common denominator in a finite tensor sum; its class in $H$ is the image of $(d+P)\otimes a^{-1}$. If this fraction maps to zero, $d/a\in J$, so $d/1\in J$ and $d\in P$, proving injectivity as well. Thus the generic fibre $V_K$ is the closure $C'_1$, by the same vanishing-ideal description as in step 2. Finally $Q$ is torsion-free over $R$: if $0\ne a\in R$ and $aq=0$, its image in the $K$-algebra $H$ is zero after division by $a$, and injectivity $Q\to H$ gives $q=0$.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 7, schematic closure of the generic closure; explicit affine quotient and fraction calculation.

proof.text: A DVR is a principal ideal domain [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] applied to $Q$ proves flatness over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], $V\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat. A finite generating set of $B$ over $A$ generates $D$ over $R$, and its images generate $Q$ over $R$, so $V\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every $d\in P$ one has $e_i(d)=0$: its image in $K$ is $e_{i,K}(d/1)=0$, and $R\to K$ is injective. Therefore the closed-fibre value of every section lies in $V_k\subseteq Y_k$. This subset is closed, since the quotient closed immersion $V\hookrightarrow Y_R$ remains closed after base change [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. It follows that $C'_0\subseteq |V_k|$.

source.place: Tag 0AUW, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat (1); Tag 01U5, morphisms-lemma-flat-characterize; BLR 5.3 Lemma 7, flatness and containment.

proof.text: If $\dim C'_1=\infty$ the required inequality is automatic. Otherwise $C'_1\ne\varnothing$ because the family is nonempty, so its dimension is an integer $r\geq0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Apply [lem-trf-flat-family-generic-dimension-bound] with integral base $\operatorname{Spec}R$, the flat locally finite type morphism $V\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ of step 4, and $r=\dim V_K=\dim C'_1$. It gives $\dim V_k\leq\dim C'_1$. Since $C'_0$ is closed in $V_k$, each chain of irreducible closed subsets of $C'_0$ is the same strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $V_k$, so $\dim C'_0\leq\dim V_k$ directly from [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Step 2 now gives $\dim C_0=\dim C'_0\leq\dim C'_1=\dim C_1$.
